title: Productionize the Helm chart (deployment/helm)
body:
## Productionize the existing Helm chart

We ship a Helm chart at [`deployment/helm/`](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/tree/main/deployment/helm), but it's currently a **minimal, dev/Minikube-oriented chart** rather than something teams can confidently run in production. This issue is to **inspect the existing chart and productionize it.**

### Current state (what's there today)

- `Chart.yaml` (`version: 0.1.0`, `appVersion: "1.16.0"` — looks stale, doesn't track the cognee release), `values.yaml`, and templates for the cognee deployment/service, an in-cluster Postgres deployment + PVC + service, and a secret.
- Single `replicas: 1` for both cognee and Postgres, hardcoded into the templates.
- `resources` sets **limits only, no requests**; no liveness/readiness/startup probes; no `securityContext`.
- LLM/DB config and credentials are passed largely as **plaintext env from `values.yaml`**; the secret value is templated straight from values (`LLM_API_KEY | b64enc`), so secrets live in the release/values.
- `ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL` is **hardcoded to `"false"`** in the deployment.
- Postgres runs as a plain **Deployment** (not a StatefulSet) and is not optional — no toggle for an external/managed database.
- No Ingress, no configurable Service type, no HPA, no PDB, no NetworkPolicy, no TLS.
- No `_helpers.tpl`, no standard `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels, no `values.schema.json`, no `NOTES.txt`, no `helm test` hooks, no CI lint/template validation. File naming is inconsistent (`secrets.yml` vs `.yaml`).

### Goal

Turn this into a **production-grade, configurable, documented chart** that a team can deploy to a real cluster with sensible defaults and override safely.

### Scope / checklist

**Reliability & workloads**
- [ ] Add liveness/readiness/startup probes for cognee (and Postgres).
- [ ] Add resource **requests** alongside limits; make them configurable.
- [ ] Make `replicaCount` configurable; document statelessness assumptions for scaling cognee.
- [ ] Convert in-cluster Postgres to a **StatefulSet**, and make it **optional** via a toggle for using an external/managed database (e.g. `postgresql.enabled` + `externalDatabase.*`). Consider depending on the upstream Bitnami/CloudNativePG chart instead of a hand-rolled deployment.
- [ ] Add `PodDisruptionBudget` and optional `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`.

**Security**
- [ ] Stop templating secret values from `values.yaml`; support **referencing an existing Secret** (`existingSecret`) and document External Secrets / sealed-secrets usage.
- [ ] Add `securityContext` / `podSecurityContext` (non-root, read-only FS where possible, drop capabilities).
- [ ] Add a `ServiceAccount` (configurable, optional creation) and stop hardcoding `ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL`.
- [ ] Optional `NetworkPolicy`.

**Networking & config**
- [ ] Add configurable `Service` type and an `Ingress` template (host, TLS, annotations, className).
- [ ] Surface all cognee env/config (LLM provider/model, vector/graph/relational DB providers, etc.) through `values.yaml` cleanly, with a `ConfigMap` where appropriate.

**Chart hygiene & quality**
- [ ] Add `_helpers.tpl` with standard naming + `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels and selectors.
- [ ] Correct `appVersion` to track the actual cognee release and document the versioning policy; add `maintainers`, `.helmignore`, `NOTES.txt`.
- [ ] Add `values.schema.json` to validate user input.
- [ ] Add `helm test` hooks (e.g. a connection/health test).
- [ ] Add CI: `helm lint`, `helm template`, and schema/manifest validation (e.g. `kubeconform`) on PRs touching the chart.
- [ ] Rewrite `deployment/helm/README.md` with install/upgrade/uninstall, a full values table, and at least one production-values example.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `helm lint` and `helm template` pass in CI; rendered manifests validate against the Kubernetes schema.
- [ ] The chart deploys cleanly with **secure defaults**, no secrets stored in `values.yaml`, and probes/resources set.
- [ ] Postgres can be toggled off in favor of an external database without editing templates.
- [ ] README documents every value and shows a realistic production override.

Happy to split this across multiple PRs — security, workloads, networking, and chart hygiene are natural independent chunks.

title: [Compliance] Add APRA CPS 234 (Information Security) framework for AWS

labels.name: compliance
labels.description: Issues/PRs related with the Compliance Frameworks

labels.name: not-planned
labels.description: Issues that are not in the Prowler roadmap.

body:
### Feature search

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and this feature has not been requested yet or is already in our [Public Roadmap](https://roadmap.prowler.com/roadmap)

### Which component would this feature affect?

Prowler CLI/SDK

### Related to specific cloud provider?

AWS

### New feature motivation

APRA's Prudential Standard CPS 234 — Information Security is mandatory for all APRA-regulated entities in Australia (banks/ADIs, general & life insurers, private health insurers, and superannuation/RSE
  licensees). It is the single most cited information-security obligation for the Australian financial sector.

  Prowler already ships asd_essential_eight_aws, but there is currently no APRA framework. Australian regulated entities running on AWS have no out-of-the-box way to benchmark their accounts against CPS
  234 with Prowler, despite it being a legal requirement for them.

### Solution Proposed

Add an APRA CPS 234 (Information Security) compliance framework for the AWS provider:
  - New framework spec: prowler/compliance/aws/apra_cps_234_aws.json — 20 requirements mapped to the operative paragraphs of CPS 234 (paras 13–36, July 2019).
    - 12 automated controls mapped to 55 existing AWS checks (IAM/MFA/password policy, encryption at rest & in transit, key management, public-exposure blocking, audit logging, threat detection, backups,
  incident-detection alarms, vulnerability testing) — no new checks required.
    - 8 manual controls for governance/process paragraphs not observable via AWS APIs (roles & responsibilities, capability, policy framework, asset classification, third-party control design, response
  plans, internal audit, APRA notification) — marked Manual, consistent with how Essential Eight handles non-automatable items.
  - New attribute model APRA_CPS234_Requirement_Attribute in prowler/lib/check/compliance_models.py, mirroring the existing ASDEssentialEight_* model (Section, ItemId, AssessmentStatus,
  CloudApplicability, Description, RationaleStatement, ImpactStatement, RemediationProcedure, AuditProcedure, AdditionalInformation, References).
  - Tests under tests/compliance/aws/.

### Use case and benefits

- Who: APRA-regulated entities and the consultants/auditors who serve them — a large, compliance-driven AWS user base.
 - Benefit: run prowler aws --compliance apra_cps_234_aws to get an instant CPS 234 posture report, with each finding mapped to the specific CPS 234 paragraph, rationale, remediation and reference —
  turning raw findings into board/regulator-ready evidence.
 - For Prowler: extends the Australian framework coverage already started with Essential Eight, and reuses existing checks (low maintenance burden, no new check logic).


### Describe alternatives you've considered

  - Generic attribute schema instead of a dedicated Pydantic model — works, but drops the rich rationale/remediation/reference fields from output; a dedicated model (as with Essential Eight/CIS) preserves
  them. Happy to go either way per maintainer preference.
  - Other tools (Steampipe/Powerpipe mods, AWS Config conformance packs, hand-rolled audits) — these exist piecemeal but none give Prowler users native CPS 234 coverage, and most require separate tooling.
  - Doing nothing / manual mapping — every AU entity re-deriving the CPS 234 → AWS mapping by hand is duplicated effort and error-prone.

### Additional context

- Reference standard: APRA CPS 234 Information Security (July 2019, current/in-force) — https://www.apra.gov.au/sites/default/files/cps_234_july_2019_for_public_release.pdf
 - I have the framework already drafted and locally validated: parses against Compliance, conforms to the new attribute model, 0 dangling check references (all 55 verified against Prowler 5.29.2),
  paragraph references verified against the official standard, 6 tests passing, and it runs end-to-end against a real AWS account.
 - Note: this is distinct from CPS 230 (Operational Risk Management, 2025) — a separate standard I'd be glad to follow up with if this is welcome.
 - Ready to open the PR as soon as I have a green light. Thank You.

- The flag and behavior are documented in the integration README.

title: Feature: new environment variable PIP_AUDIT_IGNORE_VULN
body:
### Pre-submission checks

- [x] I am **not** reporting a new vulnerability or requesting a new vulnerability identifier. These **must** be reported or managed via upstream dependency sources or services, not this repository.
- [x] I agree to follow the [PSF Code of Conduct](https://www.python.org/psf/conduct/).
- [x] I have looked through the open issues for a duplicate request.

### What's the problem this feature will solve?

CI breaks when new vulnerabilities are reported, and it’s tedious to modify CI to add & ignore vulnerabilities. Having an environment variable would make managing ignoring vulnerabilities easier and more flexible.

### Describe the solution you'd like

A new environment variable `PIP_AUDIT_IGNORE_VULN` which mimics the behavior of the `--ignore-vuln` command line option. The environment variable could take a space-separated list of vulnerability ids.

### Additional context

_No response_
